# Contributing

DTW-C++ is an open-source project open to both academic and commercial applications. We welcome and appreciate any contributions from the community. For our code of conduct, please refer to the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/).

## Opening issues

We track bugs and feature requests in GitHub issues. Open an issue for any bug report or improvement idea, or re-open a closed issue if it still needs attention. Issues labelled `good first issue` are good starting points.

## Pull requests (PRs)

We welcome [GitHub pull requests](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/creating-a-pull-request):

1. Open an issue describing the problem and your planned approach, if one does not already exist.
2. We do not have a contributor license agreement yet; but please just agree that your contributions will be publicly open.
3. Fork the repository and implement your change following the [coding conventions](conventions.md).
4. Include tests covering the bug fix or feature, and steps to reproduce any bug fixed.
5. Squash your work into a single commit with a clear message and open a PR referencing the issue.

The core team will review your PR as soon as possible. If accepted, we will add you to the [list of contributors](contributors.md). See [`develop/`](https://github.com/Battery-Intelligence-Lab/dtw-cpp/tree/main/develop) for further details.
